title: A date macro embedded in a longer string is substituted by the client resolver and left literal by the server resolver
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTRf6qBRCqPh4JZaZL

## What was read

Read during the contract review of PR #35743 (record 7031292409), not part of that diff, at `origin/main` `03bce5c22`:

- Client: `resolveDateMacros` in `ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts:186-205` first tries a whole-value match, then runs a global replace (`/\$?\{([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\}/g`) over the string, so a value such as `'from {today} on'` comes back with the macro substituted.
- Server: `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts:86-90` states that only a value that is entirely a placeholder is one, and "values that merely CONTAIN braces are left untouched".

So the same filter value resolves differently depending on which side resolves it. The published query skill (`skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md`, the "Unknown tokens" paragraph) teaches the server reading for every token: a value that merely contains braces is a literal. That sentence is exact for session tokens and the period key on both sides, and for date macros on the server only.

## Question for triage

Which side is the contract: should the client stop substituting embedded date macros, or is embedded substitution a supported client-only behaviour that the skill and docs should name? Not measured here: who relies on the embedded form today (dashboard widget titles, URL templates), and whether a test pins it.

## Done when

- One reading is chosen and both resolvers, or the skill sentence, agree with it.

Bare card for triage; not claimed, not started. Source: seat request on area b1-D.
